findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/integration/budget-pad-lift-off.png (tank farm at about x 1400-1800, y 740-940 and crawlerway at x 2040-2400, y 820-980 of the 2560 px frame); C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/integration/shadows-pad-with-the-site-and-the-vehicle-low-sun.png
findings.defect: Under the real terrain the launch complex does not sit on the ground. The tank-farm slab hovers above the slope as a thin plate with its pipe run leaving the corner as a bridge in mid-air, the crawlerway is a razor-thin strip floating over the terrain with a dark underside edge, and the whole pad sits on a hard-edged, perfectly circular grey disc. None of the package's own 97 screenshots can show this: the vehicle lab puts the site on a relief-free sphere (padElevation: () => 0), and the hand-off lists a terrain-derived elevation as untested.
findings.realReference: A real complex is graded into the land: the pad is a raised mound or cut with sloped embankments, tank farms sit on bermed, levelled pads with retaining walls, pipe lines run on stanchions of varying height that follow the ground, crawlerways are a river-rock roadbed on an embankment, and every edge meets soil with a shoulder, a drainage ditch and tyre-worn dirt. No slab ever shows its underside.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/siteFeature.ts:87-89 resolves ONE padElevation for the whole site and every structure is placed on that plane, while the site reaches 330 m and more from the pad (crawlerway length 330, pipe runs 256 and 278 m, two tank farms in data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.structures.json). The terrain feature only paints/flattens a disc of min(apronRadiusM, pad.flatRadius) (src/render/terrain/feature.ts:311-313) although data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.json says flatRadius 450 / blendRadius 900. Slabs are thin (apron thickness 0.3 m in the structures file) and footings reach well under a metre below the pad plane, so any drop in the terrain exposes an underside.
findings.fixDirection: Give createSiteFeature a per-structure ground-height callback (ENU offset -> terrain height) and place each structure at its own ground height; build every slab, kerb and footing with a skirt or embankment that goes several metres below grade; make pipe runs stand on stanchions whose length follows the terrain and drape the crawlerway over it (or on a graded embankment mesh). In parallel file a request so the terrain flattening and blend really cover the site footprint and the pad disc has a graded, irregular, soil-blended edge instead of a circle. Add an integration screenshot from a low side angle of the tank farm and crawlerway and an assertion on the largest slab-to-terrain gap.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vehicle/stage-capsule-space.png; capsule-windows.png; capsule-hatch.png; stage-lander-space.png; stage-ascent-space.png; staging-05-m-3-separation.png to staging-10-mains.png (same folder)
findings.defect: The capsule, the hero object of the game, reads as a kiln or a bathroom wall: a cone and a cylindrical 'chimney' covered in cream square tiles with wide dark grout lines and a checkerboard of tan tiles, topped by a rolled lip. The tile pattern stays readable from 15 m (staging frames), there is no sheen, no panel structure and no forward-bay or parachute-cover geometry, and the apex tunnel is tiled like a chimney pot with no docking hardware.
findings.realReference: Apollo CM: mirror-like aluminised Kapton tape in long strips, with wrinkles and seams, reflecting the Earth and black sky. Orion: black back-shell tiles under silver aluminised tape, a few large trapezoidal panels, sharp panel breaks, forward bay cover with gores. Dragon: smooth white panels with hairline seams. In all of them tile gaps are about 1 mm and invisible beyond a metre, tone varies by 2-3 % at most, and the top is a docking tunnel with a ring, latches and a hatch, not a tiled pipe.
findings.likelyCause: tools/vehicle/bake-textures.ts tile() (about lines 283-360): gap albedo 0.36 over a half-width of 0.007-0.016 tile (2.5 to 6 mm dark joints on a 180 mm tile, written into the albedo so they survive mip-mapping), 12 % 'toasted' tiles (kind > 0.88: shade -0.07, warm 0.04) plus 7 % bright replacements; material 'tile-white' in src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:77 is a plain rough dielectric; tileSize 0.18 and the courses in src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:166-176; the tunnel and its lip use the same shell material.
findings.fixDirection: Pick one real back-shell vocabulary and build it: either aluminised-tape strips (metallic 1, roughness about 0.25, anisotropic along the strip, strip seams and wrinkles in the normal map) or large white/black panels 0.4 to 0.8 m with hairline gaps carried by the normal/AO map only (gap albedo contrast under 10 %, fading with mip). Cut tile-to-tile tone variation to 2-3 % and drop the tan checker. Model the forward bay: parachute compartment gores, apex cover seam, docking ring with petals/latches and tunnel hatch; give the shoulder a visible seal band and RCS ports with scarfed recesses rather than black blocks.

findings.defect: The lander's insulation does not read as foil. Under the low lunar sun (the landing view) the silver blanket is black-and-white static like granite or camouflage and the gold lobes are mottled gold leaf; close up it is a Voronoi crackle that looks like hammered brass or reptile skin, stretched tight over mathematically perfect cylinders with a single dark line for a seam. The hand-off calls this 'noisy'; a player would call it a broken texture.
findings.realReference: Apollo LM and modern lander MLI is a loose, baggy film: large pillows and creases 10 to 40 cm across, taped overlapping panels with visible tape seams, grommets and stand-off buttons, sagging between fasteners so the silhouette is never a clean cylinder. Each crease is a long, sharp, mirror-bright glint; between glints the film is a smooth dark or amber mirror of the sky and the ground, not pixel-scale speckle. Gold is amber Kapton with a deep orange cast in the folds; black Kapton and bare aluminised panels sit beside it.
findings.likelyCause: tools/vehicle/bake-textures.ts mli() (about lines 369-400): the normal map is two Worley cell layers (20x34 and 8x13 cells per 1.1 m tile), each cell a flat tilted facet, so the highlight is quantised per cell; with metallic 0.85-0.9 and roughness 0.38-0.4 ('mli-gold', 'mli-silver' in src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:79-80) every 4-10 cm facet flips between sun, sky and black. The hull under it is an exact lathe (src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts), so there is no geometric sag, overlap or panel edge.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the cell facets by a crease-based height field (ridged, directional folds at 5-40 cm plus fine crinkle), baked with a roughness map that is low on the film and higher on tape; add real geometry: blanket panels as separately offset, slightly pillowed patches with overlapping edges, tape strips, buttons, and 1-3 cm of low-frequency displacement so silhouettes wobble. Add a pre-filtered far representation (roughness raised from normal variance per mip, i.e. Toksvig/LEAN, beyond the Kaplanyan term) so at 10 m and more the blanket is a broad streaky sheen instead of speckle. Re-shoot at sun elevation 5, 16 and 40 degrees.

findings.defect: The ablating heat shield is one flat, evenly coloured pale-orange disc with a hard edge, like an unlit lamp shade: no gradient from the stagnation point to the shoulder, no texture, no spill of light onto the back shell, compression pads glowing the same colour. In the integration reentry frame it is a uniform white ellipse while the back shell stays cool cream.
findings.realReference: Entry footage and arc-jet tests: the shield is white-yellow where heating peaks (stagnation region and the windward shoulder), falling to orange and dull red toward the lee side, with brighter streaks along tile gaps and where ablation products stream off; the glow lights the back shell and trailing wake, and the pattern flickers.
findings.likelyCause: The shield is one instance with one temperature (src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:689-692) and the mesh shader adds blackbody(T) uniformly per instance (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:181-182); there is no per-vertex or textured heat distribution and the sim's 3100 K saturates the tone curve.
findings.fixDirection: Split the shield into concentric and windward/leeward bands with their own temperatures (as the engines do with hotA / hotB), or drive an emissive texture (radial falloff, gap streaks, noise) through emissiveScale from the temperature; offset the hot spot toward the windward shoulder from the angle of attack; let the shoulder and first tile courses of the back shell take a fraction of the glow; register a capsule-shaped local light so the back shell and wake are lit.

findings.defect: Pristine, the heat shield looks like a paper parasol: khaki with pale concentric rings and radial lines that converge into thin wedges at the centre, and a knife-edge shoulder. 'Charred' is the same picture with grey radial sunbeam stripes; the pale seam lines stay bright and nothing is pitted, flaked or blackened. After entry the back shell is still clean cream with a faint grey smear at the bottom course: a flown capsule looks unflown.
findings.realReference: Avcoat (Apollo, Orion): tan-grey blocks roughly 0.2 to 0.6 m in a non-radial layout with thin dark filled seams, or a fine honeycomb. After entry: near-black to chocolate char with lighter ash-grey patches, pitting, exposed honeycomb, eroded seams and flow streaks that fan from the stagnation point (offset from centre). The back shell is scorched brown-black on the windward side and around the shoulder, tape is discoloured and peeling, windows are filmed over, RCS ports are sooted.
findings.likelyCause: tools/vehicle/bake-textures.ts ablator() (lines 242-277) is a 3x3 block grid that the lathe maps in polar UVs, so blocks become rings and wedges. Char is only the shader's uniform soot tint (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:160-163) weighted per vertex by shieldChar() / scorch() in src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:180-195, which hash the azimuth into 18/48/144 bins (hence stripes) and give the back shell a floor of 0.18 with a 1.6 power falloff. The auto exposure of a black frame then lifts the darkened surface back up.
findings.fixDirection: Lay the shield blocks out in a planar/hex layout independent of the lathe UVs, darker and less yellow. Add a second, charred texture set (albedo, normal, roughness) and blend to it by ablatorFraction through a noise threshold so char arrives in patches with eroded seams; drive streak direction from an off-centre stagnation point. On the back shell use a soot/scorch streak texture along flow lines from the shoulder, heavier windward, around RCS ports, windows and the hatch seal, and dull the surface (kill sheen) where scorched. Shoot the charred views with a fixed exposure next to the pristine ones.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vehicle/engines-clean.png; engines-sooted.png; stage-m1-aft-space.png; stage-m2-aft-space.png; pad-engine-section.png; site-apron.png (wall under the launch mount, x 520-760, y 250-330); closeup-brushed-steel.png; fairing-petal-outside.png; pad-arms-retracted.png; site-crew-arm-from-tower.png
findings.defect: Stippled dots all over the picture: the nozzle extensions look perforated (white or dark dots along every bell lip), access doors are drawn as dotted rectangles, the tower lattice sparkles, and shadow edges on the launch-mount wall and tower beams are a coarse checker of dots covering areas a metre across. It appears in at least ten of the acceptance views, including every engine view, so those views cannot be judged as they stand. How much of it a player sees is NOT established: the specs capture with a frozen noise pattern (see cause), and in live play the same pixels are a temporally dithered blend that TAA has to average, which typically shows as shimmer whenever the camera or the vehicle moves.
findings.realReference: Real hardware has continuous surfaces and shadows with a clean, soft penumbra. A shipped game hides LOD changes and shadow filtering completely.
findings.likelyCause: The mesh system blends LODs over a static size band (src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:652-659, LOD_FADE_BAND 0.15): any model whose projected size sits within +/-15 % of a lodPixels threshold is drawn permanently as two interleaved LODs with a blue-noise discard (lines 130-134), so a camera parked near the pad keeps the engines (lodPixels [200, 44], src/render/vehicle/parts/engine.ts:381) in the band for as long as it stays. Shadow penumbrae use the same noise (src/render/core/shaders/chunksLighting.ts:507). The specs call settle() (tests/browser/vehicle/lab.ts:14-17), which switches the renderer to deterministic mode; there the blue-noise offset is pinned to [0, 0] (src/render/core/renderer.ts:527 and :618), so 48 settled frames average nothing and the pattern is frozen into the picture. LOD0 and LOD1 surfaces also do not coincide, which is what makes the dots stand out.
findings.fixDirection: First establish the truth: capture the engine, apron-wall and tower views in live (non-deterministic) mode, static and with a slow camera move, and look for shimmer. Make the acceptance capture show what a player sees (keep the noise sequence running while settling, or average a full noise cycle). Independently of that, request a time-based LOD transition with hysteresis from the core (cross-fade for about 0.3 s when the LOD changes, then draw exactly one LOD) instead of a standing blend band; in the package make LOD1 circumscribe the same surface as LOD0 on bells and skins and set lodPixels so the 5-150 m hero distances are not near a threshold. If the dotted shadow on the wall under the launch mount survives live capture it is the shadow filter and needs a core request.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vehicle/pad-stack-tower-15m-up.png (dotted diagonal from x 140, y 0 to x 560, y 490); perf-tower-1440p.png; site-overview-noon.png and site-far-800m.png (pipe runs); site-overview-night.png; compare adhoc-f1-overview.png
findings.defect: Thin linear structures break up. From the tower the catenary wire is a row of dots across the sky; in the overviews the wires are missing altogether (the three 165 m masts stand unconnected, where the earlier adhoc-f1-overview.png still had them), and the pipe runs across the site are wobbly dashed lines with bright and dark beads. (The small black disc in the sky of pad-stack-tower-15m.png and -up.png is the lab planet's unlit Moon, not this package.)
findings.realReference: In photographs of LC-39B the catenary wires are continuous hair-thin lines that fade with distance but never dot, and cross-country pipe lines read as continuous, slightly glinting lines with regular supports.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts:585-614: the wire is a 0.035 m tube (LOD0), 0.112 m (LOD1) and nothing at LOD2 with lodPixels [2500, 900]; sub-pixel tubes are rasterised without coverage, and inside the LOD1-to-nothing band the wire is dither-discarded (with the noise frozen by the specs' deterministic capture this is the row of dots; live it will be a faint or flickering wire, to be checked). pad.pipeRun (src/render/vehicle/site/pad.ts) has the same problem with 0.28-0.5 m pipes, supports and expansion loops beyond a few hundred metres.
findings.fixDirection: Draw wires and far pipe runs as camera-facing ribbons whose width is clamped to about 1.2 px and whose opacity/brightness carries the true sub-pixel coverage (or thicken with distance and darken toward the sky colour); never drop them to nothing while the masts are visible. Give pipe runs a far LOD that merges pipes, supports and loops into one continuous strip.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vehicle/stage-m1-space.png; stage-m2-space.png; stage-m3-space.png; stage-ascent-space.png; staging-00-stack.png to staging-04-m-2-separation.png; pad-stack-300m.png
findings.defect: Seen alone, the stages are primitives with a texture: M-1 is a clean white tube with one black band (a pen), M-2 an orange tube with a dozen pale blotches (a cardboard roll), M-3 a stubby can whose white foam reads as leather or stucco above a chrome band (a vacuum flask), the ascent stage a foil drum with a blank white rectangle for a radiator. From 40 m nothing breaks the silhouette on the visible side and there is no weathering, staining or stencilling at readable scale.
findings.realReference: S-IC / S-II / S-IVB, Shuttle ET, Centaur, Falcon 9: external LOX feedlines and pressurisation lines standing off the barrel on brackets, cable trays on two or more azimuths, ullage and retro motor fairings, antenna and vent blisters, stringer-stiffened intertanks and skirts with real relief and shadow, weld lands as slightly different sheen bands, foam with lathe spray rings every few centimetres, sanded close-outs, ice-frost ramps, darker UV-aged patches, grime trails below vents, stencils and roll patterns.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts builds the barrel as one lathe with a single raceway azimuth and small fittings; foam relief is only the normal map of 'foam-orange' / 'foam-white' (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:70-74, tile 9.6 m) whose popcorn cells are 5-8 cm and uniform, and the close-out patches are low-contrast blobs in the albedo; the radiator on the ascent stage is a flat panel (src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts).
findings.fixDirection: Add silhouette-breaking systems from parameters in the visual files: a full-length feedline with brackets and bellows on M-2 and M-1, a second cable tray, motor fairings, vent and antenna blisters, intertank stringers as geometry at LOD0/1. Rework foam: spray-pass rings 3-6 cm in the normal map, sharper machined close-outs, metre-scale tone drift of +/-10 %, darker aged streaks under protuberances; shrink the bump on M-3's white foam so it stops reading as leather. Give white paint weld-land sheen bands, stencils and light streaking. Detail the radiator (louvres or tube-and-fin with shadow).

findings.defect: Engine faults visible from the aft: nozzle interiors are a mottled terracotta, like flower pots or cork; the six M-2 vacuum nozzles are featureless dark-grey cones (plastic cups) with no stiffening or seams; where the regenerative bell meets the extension there is a saturated rainbow bead ring (red, purple, blue dots) that reads as fairy lights; the base heat shield has flat, bright white discs with blue balls at each engine that look unshaded.
findings.realReference: Inside a regeneratively cooled bell you see fine longitudinal tubes or channels in grey nickel/steel with a straw-to-blue tint, sooty black on kerolox or clean on methalox and hydrolox; copper shows only in the chamber above the throat. Radiatively cooled extensions (RL10-B2, Merlin Vacuum, J-2X) are thin dark shells with many circumferential stiffener rings, weld seams and a broad, low-saturation heat discolouration. Engine boots are quilted, stitched fabric that is grey-white and shaded like everything else.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/parts/engine.ts:187 passes 'copper' ([0.86, 0.5, 0.33], cast-metal ORM noise) as the gas-side material of the whole bell; the extension uses 'nozzle-ext' (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:64) on a plain lathe; 'inconel' maps heat_albedo (straw to purple to blue along v, tile 1 m) onto a band a few centimetres high; the boots use 'blanket' with soot/AO masks that leave them far brighter than the shield around them.
findings.fixDirection: Use the tube-wall normal map and a dark heat-stained nickel albedo (about 0.25-0.35, roughness 0.5) for the gas side, copper only in the chamber; add stiffener rings, seams and a broad faint tint to the extensions; widen the heat-tint transition to 0.3-1 m and cut its saturation by two thirds; darken and quilt the boots and show the gimbal hardware they cover.

findings.defect: Soot from a burn turns the white tank into what looks like polished grey metal: a smooth grey gradient with a glossy sky reflection, bounded by hard vertical and horizontal edges of rectangular panels. It reads as a material swap to steel, not as soot.
findings.realReference: A flown Falcon 9 booster: matte brown-black soot, heaviest near the engines and on the lee side, feathered upward in long vertical streaks, with clean white patches where frost shielded the LOX tank, hand-wide wipe marks and a sharp clean line at weld bands. No gloss at all.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/core/mesh/meshSystem.ts:160-163 darkens albedo and raises base roughness with soot, but the clear coat (material.params.w, written at line 188) stays at full strength, so the dark layer keeps a mirror-like coat. The weights come from src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts:93-122 (sootAt on 1 m rings up to sootTop 7 m and the skin's azimuth columns), i.e. per-vertex on a 0.2 by 1 m grid, which gives the rectangular blocks.
findings.fixDirection: Either request that the core scale clear coat by (1 - soot) and (1 - frost), or draw soot as its own matte layer the way the rime layer is drawn. Modulate the weight with a streak texture (vertical fbm streaks, drips below fittings, clean masks where frost sat) at 5 cm resolution instead of bare vertex weights, tint it brown-black, and let it reach much higher than 7 m on the lee side.

findings.defect: The pad deck, the closest thing a player sees before launch, is a stage set. Rainbirds are red cones on grey poles (toy megaphones). Hold-down clamps are flat extruded white pylons with a yellow chequered tip that merely touch the skirt. The deck is a featureless blue-grey plane with a painted ring and a plain round hole. The stair to the deck is a black zig-zag of flat plates with no treads, landings or rails. Swing arms end in a block with four pipe stubs that connect to nothing: no hoses, cables, purge ducts, drip trays or vapour. The underside of the walkways is a black slab.
findings.realReference: SLS / Saturn / Falcon pads: rainbirds are large galvanised or red goose-neck pipes 0.6-1 m in diameter with flattened fan nozzles and flanged bases; hold-down arms are massive cast or welded links with pins, hydraulic cylinders, shrouds and scorched blast covers; the deck is steel plate and refractory concrete with seams, bolt heads, rust runs, scorch fans and standing water; stairs have open-grate treads, stringers and yellow rails; umbilicals carry bundles of flex hoses, cable looms and frosted cryo lines with venting vapour.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/site/pad.ts:367-376 (rainbird = rod + frustum), :399 (stair = beam plates 1.1 m by 0.06 m), the deck is one flat surface of 'concrete' whose 18 m tile has no fine grain; padClamp in src/render/vehicle/parts/structures.ts:339; swing arms in src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts carry lines but nothing spans the last metre to the vehicle. The hand-off names clamps, rainbirds and missing hoses as weak; they are in the first frame of every launch.
findings.fixDirection: Model rainbirds as flanged elbow pipes with fan nozzles and supports; rebuild the clamps as pinned link arms with actuator, shroud and blast shield, visibly bearing on hard points of the skirt; panel the deck (plates, hatches, refractory pads, drain grates, scorch and rust masks, fine-grain detail normal); build the stair with treads, landings and rails; hang catenary hose and cable bundles from each umbilical plate to the vehicle's plates (they retract with the arm) and add grating with see-through openings or a framed underside to the walkways.

findings.defect: The complex reads as a model railway set: a handful of objects on bare ground with nothing between them. Storage spheres are perfectly smooth white balls on stilts with one stripe; the apron and flame trench are spotless (no blast scorch, no rust or water staining, no tyre marks); pipes are flat saturated coral red or uniform chrome with no flanges, insulation breaks or labels; the deluge main dead-ends in a building wall; there are no roads, fences, berms, drainage, lighting-mast guy lines, cameras, vehicles or clutter.
findings.realReference: LC-39B / SLC-40 aerials: a blackened, rust-streaked flame trench and scorched apron fanning from the exhaust opening; spheres built of welded gore plates with visible seam pattern, streaks from the vents, spiral stairs, top platforms, vent stacks and thick vacuum-jacketed lines; perimeter road and fence, crushed-stone crawlerway, blast berms, retention ponds, camera towers, parked service vehicles, cable trenches with covers.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/vehicle/site/farm.ts:19-37 (sphereTank is one lathe with a decal region; no gore seams or staining), pad.ts apron and trench weathering weights are mild and symmetric, pipe materials are 'paint-red' and 'steel-brushed' untextured (materials.ts), and data/defs/sites/ka-lae-lc1.structures.json holds only 25 structures.
findings.fixDirection: Add gore-plate seams, vent streaks, stair and top platform to the spheres; burn the trench, deflector and apron with a directional scorch and rust mask centred on the exhaust path (strongest in the trench, fanning 60-80 m); add flanges, supports, insulation bands and stencils to pipes and route the deluge main round the building; add generators for perimeter road, fence, berms, camera towers, cable trench covers and a few parked vehicles, placed from the structures file.

findings.defect: Night lighting is a game-engine point light, not a floodlit pad. A warm circular pool with a visible radial cut-off lies on the ground; the vehicle is no brighter than the masts; nothing casts a shadow from the lamps (rocket, tower and buildings throw none); lamp heads are white blobs with no beam. On the Moon the lander's light is a soft white blob on the ground in front of a black, unlit lander, the legs cast no shadow in it and no lamp fixture is visible.
findings.realReference: Night launch photographs: banks of xenon searchlights throw crossing blue-white beams through the haze onto a vehicle that is the brightest object in frame (nearly clipped white), with hard multiple shadows of the tower on the vehicle and of the vehicle on the ground, hundreds of small work lights on every tower level, and deep black beyond. A lander's landing lights give a hard-edged cone with crisp leg shadows.
findings.likelyCause: LocalLight in src/core/contracts/render.ts:428-437 offers only unshadowed 'point' and 'capsule' kinds; the site and vessel features push points (src/render/vehicle/siteFeature.ts:235, src/render/vehicle/vesselFeature.ts:374), so the floodlights' tiltDeg has no effect, the 260 m range ends abruptly, and the cap of 8 site lights leaves most lamps as emissive only. Lamps on 34 m poles at 700,000 cd sit closer to the ground than to the vehicle.
findings.fixDirection: File a core request for spot lights (cone, smooth range window) with at least a few shadowed slots; aim spots at the vehicle from the pole banks and from the tower, raise their intensity until the vehicle exposes near white while the ground falls off, add many low-power emissive work lights on tower levels, and give lamp heads a visible lens with glare. Ask the atmosphere package for beam scattering. For the lander: a visible lamp housing, a shadowed spot aimed at the touchdown area, and some bounce onto the descent stage.

findings.defect: Frost reads as a thin coat of whitewash: soft-edged blotches in polygonal shapes that grey out the logo and lettering, almost no brightness or texture change on the white paint, no build-up toward the tank bottom and no vapour.
findings.realReference: A loaded LOX tank is brilliant matte white, visibly brighter than the paint, with a crisp frost line at the dome welds, thicker rime low on the barrel, bare streaks where ice has slid off, sheets peeling at lift-off and a constant curtain of condensation fog rolling down the skin.
findings.likelyCause: The rime layer is a dithered offset copy of the skin with patch outlines on the 0.2 by 0.5 m lathe grid (src/render/vehicle/parts/stage.ts around line 358), material 'frost' at albedo 0.9-0.97 over paint at 0.8 (materials.ts:86).
findings.fixDirection: Cut patch edges with a noise mask at centimetre scale, raise frost albedo contrast and sparkle (fine normal detail, lower roughness glints), thicken it toward the aft dome and below fittings, and hand the vfx package anchor points for vent fog and falling ice.

findings.defect: The top of the stack is clean primitives. The lander fairing closes in a saturated brown dome (reads as a chocolate muffin or a rusty ball) on which the white boost-cover cone is perched; the escape motor is a white cylinder with four plain black cones; the fairing petal is a spotless white label with no edge thickness, rails or fasteners.
findings.realReference: Cork and ablative close-outs on fairings are light tan and usually painted white with visible trowel marks and panel joints; the Apollo SLA is a faceted cone of four panels with hinge and pyro rails. Abort motors show a composite case, a nozzle manifold with canted, fluted nozzles, raceways and attach fittings.
findings.likelyCause: 'cork' albedo and the dome profile in the fairing generator (src/render/vehicle/parts/payload.ts, data/defs/visuals/parts/meridian-lander-fairing.json); LES nozzles are frustums in 'phenolic' with no manifold (payload.ts les.tower).
findings.fixDirection: Lighten and desaturate the cork (or paint it white with tan showing at joints), add panel joints, separation rails with pyro housings and edge thickness to the petals, and give the escape motor a manifold, nozzle throats and exit lips, raceway and structural skirt.

findings.defect: Windows are flat black voids with no glass: no reflection, no inner panes or frame depth. Each window sits in a rectangular patch of differently aligned tiles that reads as a sticker; one frame is polished with bolts while its neighbour is black and visibly faceted at the corners; the hatch seal is a black tube laid on top of the tiles.
findings.realReference: Spacecraft windows are multi-pane: an outer pane with a bright, sharp reflection of Earth or sky, a visible gap, inner panes and a dark interior with lit panel glints; the surround is a machined frame flush with the TPS, and hatch seals are recessed gaps with a thin gasket line.
findings.likelyCause: 'glass' is opaque, albedo 0.012 (src/render/vehicle/materials.ts:90) and the lab's orbit environment gives it nothing to reflect toward space; close-out tiles use planarUv() in src/render/vehicle/parts/capsule.ts:279-283; frames are low-segment extrusions and metal frames go black when they reflect empty sky.
findings.fixDirection: Model the window as outer pane, reveal and a dark inner pane with a faint emissive cabin glow; make sure the pane picks up the planet in the probe; raise corner segments; blend close-out tiles into the courses; recess the hatch gap instead of laying a tube on the surface.

findings.view: C:/dev/fable-space-game/out/screens/vehicle/stage-m2-aft-space.png (the 'M-2' marking); pad-stack-tower-15m.png (coloured rectangles on the intertank); site-crew-arm-from-tower.png (signs); closeup-clearcoat-paint.png
findings.defect: Markings give the CGI away: 'M-2' printed across the corrugated skirt is broken up and partly unreadable; small green, yellow and grey rectangles on the intertank look like colour chips; the tower signs are flawless vector boards; paint is perfectly clean with faint regular vertical banding.
findings.realReference: Stencilled markings on corrugation follow the ribs with slight overspray and remain legible; real placards are small text blocks; signs are bolted sheet with fading, streaks and fixings; paint shows touch-ups, handling marks and streaks below fittings.
findings.likelyCause: Decals are opaque atlas rectangles cut into the lathe grid (hand-off deviation 5), so on corrugated skin the rectangle is sampled across ribs; placard decals are too small for the atlas resolution; the paint normal map tiles at 0.6 m with visible period.
findings.fixDirection: Put stage markings on smooth bands or project them along the rib crests; raise placard resolution or drop them at distance; add edge wear, streaks and fixings to signs; add a low-frequency grime/streak layer and break the 0.6 m paint tile with a second scale.

findings.defect: Every space view is lit like a product shot: sunlit white paint sits at mid-grey (about 160 of 255), the light is frontal and soft, and the shadow side is filled with strong blue. None of the package's pictures was taken under the real sky, atmosphere or terrain, so the acceptance set cannot show how the hardware looks in play (the one integration frame in orbit, out/screens/integration/budget-leo.png, looks markedly better at distance).
findings.realReference: Orbital photography: sunlit white is at or near clipping with small hard specular glints, the terminator on a cylinder is abrupt, and shadows are near black unless Earth fills the opposite hemisphere.
findings.likelyCause: The lab's analytic environment (labs/vehicle/labEnv.ts, kind 'orbit') and auto exposure on a mostly black frame; the specs use sun directions close to the camera axis (tests/browser/vehicle/screens.spec.ts SUN_SPACE).
findings.fixDirection: Add a set of acceptance views shot in the integration lab (pad at noon and dusk, LEO with Earth in frame, lunar surface, reentry, splashdown) with side and three-quarter sun and fixed exposure, and judge materials there; keep the vehicle lab for geometry checks.

findings.defect: Tower and crew arm are untextured-looking grey and white: beams meet with no gusset plates, bolts or weld beads, every member is the same flat grey, the tunnel and white room are plain white boxes with black window rectangles, and there is no rust, streaking or safety marking beyond yellow rails.
findings.realReference: Fixed service structures are galvanised or grey-painted steel with gusseted joints, bolt patterns, rust blooms at joints, drip streaks, cable trays, conduit, signage, hose reels and scorch on the vehicle side.
findings.likelyCause: Members are rods/beams in 'galvanised' or 'paint-grey' with uniform masks (src/render/vehicle/site/tower.ts); no joint geometry and no weathering mask by height or exposure.
findings.fixDirection: Add gusset plates and bolt groups at LOD0 joints, vary member tone, add rust/drip masks at joints and scorch on the vehicle-facing side, glaze the tunnel windows with reflective panes and add cable trays and conduit along the arm.

findings.defect: On the Moon the lander's shadow has a soft, wobbly edge and strut shadows smear near the feet; the broken leg is hard to tell from an intact one (a slight kink, the pad still resting flat).
findings.realReference: Apollo surface photographs: shadows are razor sharp within several metres of the object and pure black; a collapsed strut is visibly buckled with the pad twisted or lifted.
findings.likelyCause: Vessel shadows are cast from LOD1 / LOD2 caster batches (hand-off section 2) into cascades whose texel size is too coarse at this distance; brokenLegPose uses a 16 degree splay and a 38 degree knee in the part frame (src/render/vehicle/parts/lander.ts).
findings.fixDirection: Cast the active vessel's near cascade from LOD0 for landing gear and tighten the penumbra on airless bodies (core request if needed); exaggerate the broken pose (buckled strut, tilted pad, crushed honeycomb exposed).
